description: Comprehensive question bank on Emerging Technology (Chapter 13.3) for FDA & SDA examinations. Covers AI, ML, Big Data, Blockchain, IoT, Robotics, GIS, Remote Sensing, Indian initiatives, and comparison topics.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is Artificial Intelligence (AI)?

options.A: A field of computer science concerned with building systems that perform tasks commonly associated with human intelligence
options.B: A hardware device used for storing large databases
options.C: A programming language used for web development
options.D: A network protocol for connecting physical devices

questions.explanation: AI is a field of computer science concerned with building systems that perform tasks commonly associated with human intelligence, such as learning, reasoning, perception, language understanding, problem-solving and decision support.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is the main objective of AI?

options.A: To replace all human workers in government offices
options.B: To develop systems that can perform intelligent tasks, assist people, automate suitable processes and support decisions based on data and programmed objectives
options.C: To create only physical robots for manufacturing
options.D: To eliminate the need for data storage

questions.explanation: The main objective of AI is to develop systems that can perform intelligent tasks, assist people, automate suitable processes and support decisions based on data and programmed objectives.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: Who is widely known as the father of Artificial Intelligence?

options.A: Alan Turing

questions.explanation: John McCarthy is widely known as the father of Artificial Intelligence. He coined the term Artificial Intelligence and helped organise the 1956 Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: In which year was the term 'Artificial Intelligence' introduced at the Dartmouth workshop?
questions.explanation: The term Artificial Intelligence was introduced in connection with the Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence in 1956.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: Who were among the organisers/proposers of the 1956 Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence?

options.A: John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester and Claude Shannon
options.B: Alan Turing, John von Neumann, Claude Shannon and Arthur Samuel
options.C: John McCarthy, Alan Turing, Geoffrey Hinton and Yann LeCun
options.D: Marvin Minsky, Arthur Samuel, John Hopfield and Geoffrey Hinton

questions.explanation: John McCarthy, together with Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester and Claude Shannon, was among the organisers/proposers of the 1956 Dartmouth project.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is an AI system?

options.A: A machine-based system that infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments
options.B: A purely mechanical device without any software
options.D: A network router used for internet connectivity

questions.explanation: An AI system is a machine-based system that infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: Which of the following are major branches or areas of AI?

options.A: Machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, knowledge representation, reasoning, planning, robotics and expert systems
options.B: Only machine learning and deep learning
options.D: Only natural language processing and speech recognition

questions.explanation: Important areas include machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, knowledge representation, reasoning, planning, robotics and expert systems.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is narrow AI or weak AI?

options.A: AI designed to perform specific tasks or a limited set of tasks such as facial recognition, translation, recommendation or spam detection
options.B: AI with human-level general intelligence across all tasks
options.C: AI that exceeds human cognitive capabilities in all domains
options.D: AI that is not used in practical applications

questions.explanation: Narrow AI is designed to perform specific tasks or a limited set of tasks such as facial recognition, translation, recommendation or spam detection. Most AI systems currently in practical use are narrow AI.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is Artificial General Intelligence (AGI)?

options.A: AI designed for a single specific task
options.B: A proposed form of AI with broad, flexible capabilities comparable to human-level general intelligence across many different tasks
options.C: AI that is less capable than narrow AI
options.D: A type of database management system

questions.explanation: AGI is a proposed form of AI with broad, flexible capabilities comparable to human-level general intelligence across many different tasks. There is no generally accepted demonstration of fully realised AGI.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is superintelligence in AI?

options.A: AI that performs only simple calculations
options.B: A hypothetical form of AI that would substantially exceed human cognitive capabilities across a wide range of domains
options.D: AI that is slower than human intelligence

questions.explanation: Artificial superintelligence is a hypothetical form of AI that would substantially exceed human cognitive capabilities across a wide range of domains.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is generative AI?

options.A: AI models that generate new content, such as text, images, audio, video or code, in response to prompts or other inputs
options.B: AI that only classifies existing data
options.C: AI that only stores data in databases
options.D: AI that only monitors network traffic

questions.explanation: Generative AI refers to AI models that generate new content, such as text, images, audio, video or code, in response to prompts or other inputs.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a Large Language Model (LLM)?

options.A: A machine-learning model trained on large amounts of text or other data to process and generate language
options.B: A hardware device for language translation only
options.C: A database of all languages in the world

questions.explanation: An LLM is a machine-learning model trained on large amounts of text or other data to process and generate language. Many LLMs use the Transformer architecture.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a chatbot?

options.A: A software system designed to communicate with users through text or voice
options.B: A physical robot used in manufacturing
options.D: A hardware device for printing documents

questions.explanation: A chatbot is a software system designed to communicate with users through text or voice. AI chatbots may use natural language processing and machine-learning models to interpret and respond to queries.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is natural language processing (NLP)?

options.A: A branch of AI that enables computers to process, analyse, interpret and generate human language in text or speech form
options.B: A programming language used for web development
options.C: A network protocol for data transmission
options.D: A hardware component of a computer

questions.explanation: NLP is a branch of AI that enables computers to process, analyse, interpret and generate human language in text or speech form.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is computer vision?

options.A: An AI field that enables computers to interpret information from images and videos, such as identifying objects, reading text and detecting patterns
options.B: A field that enables computers to process only numerical data
options.C: A technique for compressing audio files
options.D: A method for storing data in cloud servers

questions.explanation: Computer vision is an AI field that enables computers to interpret information from images and videos, such as identifying objects, reading text and detecting patterns.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is speech recognition?

options.A: The conversion of spoken language into text or machine-readable commands
options.B: The conversion of text into spoken language
options.C: The conversion of images into text
options.D: The conversion of data into graphs

questions.explanation: Speech recognition converts spoken language into text or machine-readable commands.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is an expert system?

options.A: An AI programme that uses a knowledge base and inference rules to provide advice or decisions in a specialised domain
options.B: A physical robot used in hospitals
options.D: A type of computer operating system

questions.explanation: An expert system is an AI programme that uses a knowledge base and inference rules to provide advice or decisions in a specialised domain.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a knowledge base in an expert system?

options.A: A structured collection of facts, rules and domain knowledge used by an expert system to reason about a problem
options.B: A database of all user queries
options.C: A hardware component of a computer
options.D: A network protocol for data transmission

questions.explanation: A knowledge base is a structured collection of facts, rules and domain knowledge used by an expert system to reason about a problem.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is an inference engine?

options.A: A component that applies logical rules to facts in a knowledge base to derive conclusions or recommendations
options.B: A search engine used on the internet
options.C: A hardware device for cooling computers

questions.explanation: An inference engine applies logical rules to facts in a knowledge base to derive conclusions or recommendations.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a rule-based AI system?

options.A: An AI system that uses predefined logical rules, often expressed as IF-THEN statements, to reach conclusions or take actions
options.B: An AI system that learns only from data without any rules
options.C: An AI system that uses only neural networks
options.D: An AI system that has no decision-making capability

questions.explanation: A rule-based AI system uses predefined logical rules, often expressed as IF-THEN statements, to reach conclusions or take actions.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a recommendation system?

options.A: A system that analyses user preferences, behaviour or item characteristics to suggest relevant products, services, information or content
options.B: A system that only stores user data
options.C: A system that only deletes user data
options.D: A system that only encrypts data

questions.explanation: A recommendation system analyses user preferences, behaviour or item characteristics to suggest relevant products, services, information or content.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is predictive analytics in AI?

options.A: The use of historical and current data, statistical methods and machine-learning models to estimate future outcomes or probabilities
options.B: The analysis of only past data without any prediction
options.C: The process of deleting old data
options.D: The process of encrypting data for security

questions.explanation: Predictive analytics uses historical and current data, statistical methods and machine-learning models to estimate future outcomes or probabilities.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is explainable AI (XAI)?

options.A: Methods and techniques that help people understand why an AI system produced a particular prediction or decision
options.C: AI that is used only for teaching purposes
options.D: AI that has no decision-making capability

questions.explanation: Explainable AI refers to methods and techniques that help people understand why an AI system produced a particular prediction or decision.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is responsible AI?

options.A: The development and use of AI in ways that promote fairness, accountability, transparency, privacy, safety, reliability and respect for human rights
options.B: AI that is only used by responsible companies
options.C: AI that has no ethical considerations
options.D: AI that is used only for military purposes

questions.explanation: Responsible AI is the development and use of AI in ways that promote fairness, accountability, transparency, privacy, safety, reliability and respect for human rights.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is algorithmic bias?

options.A: When a system produces systematically unfair or distorted outcomes, often due to biased data, design choices, assumptions or deployment conditions
options.B: When an algorithm runs faster than expected
options.C: When an algorithm uses too much memory
options.D: When an algorithm is written in a specific programming language

questions.explanation: Algorithmic bias occurs when a system produces systematically unfair or distorted outcomes, often due to biased data, design choices, assumptions or deployment conditions.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a hallucination in generative AI?

options.A: An output that appears plausible but is false, unsupported or fabricated by the model
options.B: A visual display error on a computer screen
options.D: A hardware malfunction in a robot

questions.explanation: An AI hallucination is an output that appears plausible but is false, unsupported or fabricated by the model.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is human-in-the-loop AI?

options.A: AI that involves people in reviewing, guiding, validating or approving AI outputs or decisions, particularly where errors can have significant consequences
options.B: AI that operates without any human involvement
options.C: AI that is used only by humans
options.D: AI that replaces all human decision-making

questions.explanation: Human-in-the-loop AI involves people in reviewing, guiding, validating or approving AI outputs or decisions, particularly where errors can have significant consequences.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: How can AI help public administration?

options.A: By supporting document classification, translation, citizen-service chatbots, fraud-risk detection, traffic management, crop analysis, forecasting, grievance categorisation and decision support
options.C: By eliminating the need for data storage

questions.explanation: AI can support document classification, translation, citizen-service chatbots, fraud-risk detection, traffic management, crop analysis, forecasting, grievance categorisation and decision support.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: How can AI be used in Karnataka's administration?

options.A: For Kannada-language citizen assistance, analysis of agricultural and weather data, urban traffic optimisation, public-health planning, land-record document processing and prioritisation of service requests, subject to legal safeguards and human oversight
options.B: Only for automating physical manufacturing processes

questions.explanation: Potential applications include Kannada-language citizen assistance, analysis of agricultural and weather data, urban traffic optimisation, public-health planning, land-record document processing and prioritisation of service requests, subject to legal safeguards and human oversight.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What are the major risks of AI in government?

options.A: Biased decisions, inaccurate outputs, privacy violations, cyber threats, lack of explainability, automation errors, exclusion of vulnerable groups and excessive dependence on automated systems
options.D: Only the need for more office space

questions.explanation: Risks include biased decisions, inaccurate outputs, privacy violations, cyber threats, lack of explainability, automation errors, exclusion of vulnerable groups and excessive dependence on automated systems.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is Machine Learning (ML)?

options.A: A branch of AI in which computer systems learn patterns from data and use those patterns to make predictions, classifications or decisions without being explicitly programmed with a separate rule for every case
options.B: A hardware device used for storing data
options.C: A programming language used for web development
options.D: A network protocol for connecting devices

questions.explanation: Machine Learning is a branch of AI in which computer systems learn patterns from data and use those patterns to make predictions, classifications or decisions without being explicitly programmed with a separate rule for every case.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is the relationship between AI and ML?

options.A: AI is the broader field of building intelligent systems; ML is a subfield of AI that enables systems to learn patterns from data
options.B: ML is the broader field and AI is a subfield
options.C: AI and ML are the same thing
options.D: AI and ML are unrelated fields

questions.explanation: AI is the broader field of building intelligent systems. ML is a subfield of AI that enables systems to learn patterns from data.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: Who is associated with coining the term 'machine learning' in 1959?

options.A: John McCarthy

questions.explanation: Arthur Samuel is widely credited with coining the term 'machine learning' in 1959 while describing a computer programme that learned to play checkers.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a machine-learning model?

options.A: A mathematical or computational representation learned from training data and used to make predictions or decisions on new inputs
options.B: A physical prototype of a robot
options.D: A network protocol for data transmission

questions.explanation: A machine-learning model is a mathematical or computational representation learned from training data and used to make predictions or decisions on new inputs.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is training data?

options.A: The dataset used by a machine-learning algorithm to learn model parameters or patterns
options.B: The dataset used to evaluate the final model
options.C: The dataset used for testing only
options.D: The dataset used for validation only

questions.explanation: Training data is the dataset used by a machine-learning algorithm to learn model parameters or patterns.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is testing data?

options.A: A separate dataset used to evaluate how well a trained model performs on data not used to fit the model
options.B: The dataset used to train the model
options.C: The dataset used for validation only
options.D: The dataset used for data entry

questions.explanation: Testing data is a separate dataset used to evaluate how well a trained model performs on data not used to fit the model.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is validation data?

options.A: Data used during model development to tune model settings, compare candidate models and help select an appropriate model
options.B: Data used only for final testing
options.D: Data used only for data entry

questions.explanation: Validation data is used during model development to tune model settings, compare candidate models and help select an appropriate model.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is supervised learning?

options.A: A learning approach that trains a model using labelled examples, where each training input is associated with a known target or correct output
options.B: A learning approach that uses only unlabelled data
options.C: A learning approach that uses no data at all
options.D: A learning approach that uses only reinforcement signals

questions.explanation: Supervised learning trains a model using labelled examples, where each training input is associated with a known target or correct output.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What are examples of supervised learning tasks?

options.A: Classification and regression

questions.explanation: Classification and regression are common supervised learning tasks.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is classification in machine learning?

options.A: A supervised learning task in which a model predicts a discrete category or class, such as spam/not spam or eligible/not eligible
options.B: A supervised learning task in which a model predicts a numerical value
options.C: An unsupervised learning task that groups data points

questions.explanation: Classification is a supervised learning task in which a model predicts a discrete category or class, such as spam/not spam or eligible/not eligible.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is regression in machine learning?

options.A: A supervised learning task in which a model predicts a numerical value, such as rainfall amount, crop yield or house price
options.B: A supervised learning task in which a model predicts a discrete category
options.C: An unsupervised learning task that groups data points

questions.explanation: Regression is a supervised learning task in which a model predicts a numerical value, such as rainfall amount, crop yield or house price.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is clustering?

options.A: An unsupervised learning method that groups data points according to similarity or a chosen distance measure
options.B: A supervised learning method that predicts categories
options.C: A reinforcement learning method that uses rewards

questions.explanation: Clustering is an unsupervised learning method that groups data points according to similarity or a chosen distance measure.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of clustering?

options.A: Grouping villages or customers according to similar characteristics without pre-existing category labels
options.B: Predicting whether an email is spam or not spam
options.C: Predicting the price of a house
options.D: Training a robot to walk using rewards

questions.explanation: Grouping villages or customers according to similar characteristics without pre-existing category labels is an example of clustering.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is dimensionality reduction?

options.A: The process of reducing the number of variables or features in a dataset while attempting to preserve useful information
options.B: The process of increasing the number of features in a dataset
options.C: The process of deleting all data
options.D: The process of converting data into images

questions.explanation: Dimensionality reduction reduces the number of variables or features in a dataset while attempting to preserve useful information.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is semi-supervised learning?

options.A: A learning approach that uses a combination of a relatively small amount of labelled data and a larger amount of unlabelled data
options.B: A learning approach that uses only labelled data
options.C: A learning approach that uses only unlabelled data
options.D: A learning approach that uses no data

questions.explanation: Semi-supervised learning uses a combination of a relatively small amount of labelled data and a larger amount of unlabelled data.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is reinforcement learning?

options.A: A machine-learning approach in which an agent learns to choose actions by interacting with an environment and receiving rewards or penalties
options.B: A learning approach that uses only labelled data
options.C: A learning approach that uses only unlabelled data
options.D: A learning approach that uses no data

questions.explanation: Reinforcement learning is a machine-learning approach in which an agent learns to choose actions by interacting with an environment and receiving rewards or penalties.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is an agent in reinforcement learning?

options.A: The learner or decision-maker that observes an environment, selects actions and receives feedback in the form of rewards
options.B: A human supervisor who monitors the system
options.C: A hardware component of a computer

questions.explanation: An agent is the learner or decision-maker that observes an environment, selects actions and receives feedback in the form of rewards.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a reward in reinforcement learning?

options.A: A numerical feedback signal that indicates how desirable an outcome or action is according to the learning objective
options.B: A penalty for wrong actions only

questions.explanation: A reward is a numerical feedback signal that indicates how desirable an outcome or action is according to the learning objective.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is deep learning?

options.A: A subfield of machine learning that uses neural networks with multiple layers to learn complex patterns from data
options.B: A subfield of AI that uses only rule-based systems
options.C: A type of database management system
options.D: A network protocol for data transmission

questions.explanation: Deep learning is a subfield of machine learning that uses neural networks with multiple layers to learn complex patterns from data.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is an artificial neural network?

options.A: A computational model inspired loosely by biological neural systems, consisting of interconnected processing units or neurons arranged in layers
options.B: A network of physical computers connected by cables

questions.explanation: An artificial neural network is a computational model inspired loosely by biological neural systems, consisting of interconnected processing units or neurons arranged in layers.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a neuron in an artificial neural network?

options.A: A computational unit that receives inputs, applies weights and a bias, performs a calculation and passes an output through an activation function
options.B: A biological cell in the human brain
options.C: A hardware component of a computer

questions.explanation: A neuron is a computational unit that receives inputs, applies weights and a bias, performs a calculation and passes an output through an activation function.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is an activation function?

options.A: A function that transforms a neuron's input and helps a neural network model non-linear relationships
options.B: A function that activates the computer's power supply
options.C: A function that deletes old data

questions.explanation: An activation function transforms a neuron's input and helps a neural network model non-linear relationships.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a convolutional neural network (CNN)?

options.A: A neural-network architecture particularly effective for analysing grid-like data such as images, using convolutional operations to detect spatial patterns
options.B: A neural network used only for text processing
options.C: A neural network used only for audio processing
options.D: A neural network that has no layers

questions.explanation: A CNN is a neural-network architecture particularly effective for analysing grid-like data such as images, using convolutional operations to detect spatial patterns.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a recurrent neural network (RNN)?

options.A: A neural-network architecture designed to process sequences by maintaining information from earlier steps in a sequence
options.B: A neural network used only for image processing
options.C: A neural network that has no memory
options.D: A neural network that uses only rule-based logic

questions.explanation: An RNN is a neural-network architecture designed to process sequences by maintaining information from earlier steps in a sequence.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a Transformer model?

options.A: A neural-network architecture based primarily on attention mechanisms and widely used in modern language, vision and multimodal models
options.B: A hardware device for converting voltage
options.C: A type of database management system
options.D: A network protocol for data transmission

questions.explanation: A Transformer is a neural-network architecture based primarily on attention mechanisms and widely used in modern language, vision and multimodal models.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is overfitting in machine learning?

options.A: When a model learns the training data too closely, including noise or accidental patterns, and performs poorly on new data
options.B: When a model performs well on new data
options.C: When a model is too simple to capture patterns
options.D: When a model uses too little data

questions.explanation: Overfitting occurs when a model learns the training data too closely, including noise or accidental patterns, and performs poorly on new data.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is underfitting in machine learning?

options.A: When a model is too simple or insufficiently trained to capture important patterns in the data, resulting in poor performance on both training and new data
options.B: When a model performs well on training data but poorly on new data
options.C: When a model uses too much data
options.D: When a model has too many layers

questions.explanation: Underfitting occurs when a model is too simple or insufficiently trained to capture important patterns in the data, resulting in poor performance on both training and new data.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is generalisation in machine learning?

options.A: A model's ability to perform well on new, previously unseen data drawn from the relevant problem domain
options.B: A model's ability to memorise training data
options.C: A model's ability to use more features
options.D: A model's ability to run faster

questions.explanation: Generalisation is a model's ability to perform well on new, previously unseen data drawn from the relevant problem domain.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a feature in machine learning?

options.A: An input variable or measurable characteristic used by a model to make a prediction

questions.explanation: A feature is an input variable or measurable characteristic used by a model to make a prediction.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a label in supervised learning?

options.A: The known target value or category associated with a training example
options.B: An input variable used by a model

questions.explanation: A label is the known target value or category associated with a training example.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is an algorithm in machine learning?

options.A: A procedure used to learn patterns or model parameters from data
options.B: A hardware component of a computer

questions.explanation: A machine-learning algorithm is a procedure used to learn patterns or model parameters from data.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is model accuracy?

options.A: The proportion of predictions that are correct among all predictions, commonly used for classification when class distribution and error costs make it appropriate
options.B: The proportion of predicted positive cases that are actually positive
options.C: The proportion of actual positive cases correctly identified
options.D: The harmonic mean of precision and recall

questions.explanation: Accuracy is the proportion of predictions that are correct among all predictions, commonly used for classification when class distribution and error costs make it appropriate.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is precision in classification?

options.A: The proportion of predicted positive cases that are actually positive: true positives divided by all predicted positives
options.B: The proportion of actual positive cases correctly identified
options.C: The proportion of predictions that are correct among all predictions
options.D: The harmonic mean of precision and recall

questions.explanation: Precision is the proportion of predicted positive cases that are actually positive: true positives divided by all predicted positives.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is recall in classification?

options.A: The proportion of actual positive cases correctly identified: true positives divided by all actual positives
options.B: The proportion of predicted positive cases that are actually positive
options.C: The proportion of predictions that are correct among all predictions
options.D: The harmonic mean of precision and recall

questions.explanation: Recall is the proportion of actual positive cases correctly identified: true positives divided by all actual positives.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is the F1 score?

options.A: The harmonic mean of precision and recall, useful when both are important
options.B: The proportion of predictions that are correct among all predictions
options.C: The proportion of predicted positive cases that are actually positive
options.D: The proportion of actual positive cases correctly identified

questions.explanation: The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall and is useful when both are important.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is a confusion matrix?

options.A: A table that compares actual and predicted classes, commonly showing true positives, true negatives, false positives and false negatives
options.B: A matrix used for encrypting data
options.C: A matrix used for storing images
options.D: A matrix used for network routing

questions.explanation: A confusion matrix is a table that compares actual and predicted classes, commonly showing true positives, true negatives, false positives and false negatives.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is data leakage in machine learning?

options.A: When information unavailable at the time of real prediction improperly enters model training or evaluation, producing overly optimistic performance estimates
options.B: When data is accidentally deleted from a database
options.C: When data is shared with unauthorised users
options.D: When data is compressed for storage

questions.explanation: Data leakage occurs when information unavailable at the time of real prediction improperly enters model training or evaluation, producing overly optimistic performance estimates.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is model drift?

options.A: A decline or change in model performance as real-world data patterns or relationships change over time
options.B: When a model is moved from one computer to another
options.C: When a model is trained on a different dataset
options.D: When a model uses too many features

questions.explanation: Model drift is a decline or change in model performance as real-world data patterns or relationships change over time.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: How can machine learning help government administration?

options.A: By forecasting demand, identifying unusual transactions, classifying grievances, estimating service workloads, detecting patterns in public datasets and supporting agricultural or weather-related predictions
options.C: By eliminating the need for data storage

questions.explanation: ML can forecast demand, identify unusual transactions, classify grievances, estimate service workloads, detect patterns in public datasets and support agricultural or weather-related predictions.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: Why should machine-learning decisions in public services be audited?

options.A: Audits help identify bias, data errors, weak performance, privacy problems and unexplained outcomes, and support accountability and lawful decision-making
options.B: Audits are only required for financial transactions
options.C: Audits are only required for private companies
options.D: Audits are not necessary for ML systems

questions.explanation: Audits help identify bias, data errors, weak performance, privacy problems and unexplained outcomes, and support accountability and lawful decision-making.

questions.subject: Emerging Technology
questions.question: What is Big Data?

options.A: Datasets whose size, speed, diversity or complexity make them difficult to store, manage and analyse effectively using traditional data-processing systems alone
options.B: A type of database management system
options.C: A programming language used for web development
options.D: A network protocol for data transmission
